How to do itDumbbell Biceps Curl

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Middle of palm

Wrong: Wrist curled

Right: Middle of palm

Wrong: Wrist bent back

Elbow path

Right
ELBOW AT SIDE
Wrong
ELBOW BACK

Right: Upper arm by your side at the top.

Wrong: Elbow swung back behind the body to cheat the weight.

Keep the upper arms by your sides, never back, at most slightly forward on top.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbows forwardYour elbows drift forward off your sides.
  2. Shoulder takes overThe front of your shoulder takes over the lift.
Curl1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Palms forward, handle across the middle of your palm, thumb wrapped. Keep your wrist straight.

Keep the hand in line with the forearm, not bent up or down.

Common handling mistakes

  • Wrists bending up or down

    Fix: Keep the hand in line with the forearm.

  • Swinging the body

    Fix: Use a lighter dumbbell and lift with control.

  • Elbows drifting back or forward

    Fix: Keep the elbows at your sides. Never let them travel back.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your upper arm.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYour elbows move forward, which puts extra load on the front delts.

    FixKeep the elbows at your sides.

  • Usually meansYour wrists are bent up or down under load.

    FixStop and don't train through the pain. Keep the wrist straight.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Pick a weight you can curl without swinging.

  2. 2

    Stand with feet shoulder-width, knees slightly bent.

  3. 3

    Palms forward, thumbs wrapped, handle across the middle of the palm.

  4. 4

    Chest up, shoulders down and slightly back.

Risks and when to stop

  • Bent wrists under load can cause wrist discomfort.
  • Across weight training, dropped weights are the most common way people get badly hurt.

Wrist pain

Can't grip, wrist changed shape, or hand gone numb? Get it checked today.

Tingling, keeps coming back, or no better after two weeks' rest? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itPec Fly

Elbow bend

Right
SOFT ELBOWS
Wrong
BENT SHARPLY

Right: Slight, fixed elbow bend with the arms at chest height.

Wrong: Elbows bent sharply, as on the elbow-pad machine.

Keep a slight, fixed bend in the elbows.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Stops shortThe arms stop short: the handles finish well apart in front.
Close2 s
Hold2 s
Open2 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this across your chest.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe pec deck puts the front shoulder in a vulnerable position.

    FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

  • Usually meansThe weight is so heavy that your body sways or rocks.

    FixLower the weight.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the seat so the handles are at chest level.

  2. 2

    Sit back against the pad, feet flat, shoulder-width or wider.

  3. 3

    Take the handles with the elbows slightly bent.

  4. 4

    Pick a weight you can take through the full range without rocking.

  5. 5

    Upper back lifting off the pad? Go lighter.

Risks and when to stop

  • The pec deck puts the front of the shoulder in a vulnerable position.
  • Changing the technique to lift more weight can cause injury.
  • Starting with the arms behind the body may strain the shoulder.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.

Getting worse, very hard to move, or no better after two weeks? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itPlank

Hip line

Right
HIPS LEVEL
Wrong
LOW BACK SAGS

Right: No sagging low back, no hiked hips.

Wrong: Low back sagging.

Shoulder stack

Right
OVER ELBOWS
Wrong
NOT OVER ELBOWS

Right: Shoulders straight over the elbows.

Wrong: Shoulders not over the elbows.

Stack the shoulders right over the elbows, and don't shrug.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Hips hikeThe hips hike up above the shoulder-heel line.
Hold10–60 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front and sides of your belly.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYour low back is sagging.

    FixStop the exercise.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Lie face down, elbows under your shoulders, palms down.

  2. 2

    Straighten your legs, pull your toes up, brace your trunk.

  3. 3

    Lift slowly, trunk and legs stiff.

  4. 4

    Hold for the set time and keep breathing.

  5. 5

    Lower yourself down with the body still stiff.

Risks and when to stop

  • Low-back pain from a sagging low back. Can't hold it? Rest on your knees.
  • Low-back pain during the hold: stop.

Back pain

Pain, numbness, tingling or weakness in both legs? Numb genitals or anus? Bladder, bowel or sexual changes? Chest pain? Serious accident? Get emergency help now. Sudden severe or fast-worsening pain? Hot, cold, shivery or unwell? See a doctor today.

No better in a few weeks? See a doctor.

How to do itRope Triceps Pushdown

Elbow position

Right
AT YOUR SIDES
Wrong
DRIFTED FORWARD

Right: Elbows against your sides at the top.

Wrong: Elbows drifted forward, upper arms swung up.

Keep the upper arms at the sides from top to bottom.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Leaning overYou lean far over the rope or arch your back to push it down.
Press1 s
Hold1 s
Return3 s
Look closer

Grip

Hold each rope end, hands against the knobs, palms facing. Spread the ends apart at the bottom.

Fist curling toward the forearm? Keep the wrist straight.

Common handling mistakes

  • Leaning over or arching back

    Fix: Stand taller. Tilt only from the hips.

  • Elbows drifting forward or out

    Fix: Keep your elbows at your sides.

  • Rope rising too high

    Fix: Stop when your forearms are just past parallel.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the back of your upper arms.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe rope rises higher than just above parallel.

    FixStop when your forearms are just past parallel.

  • Usually meansYou lean too far forward or arch your back.

    FixStop and don't train through the pain. Stand taller, tilt only from the hips.

  • Usually meansHeavy, low-rep sets feel uncomfortable in the elbows for many.

    FixStop and don't train through the pain. Go lighter, don't lock out your elbows.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Fix the rope to the pulley at its top position.

  2. 2

    Hold each end with your hand against the knob, thumbs wrapped.

  3. 3

    Stand facing the machine, feet hip-width or staggered, torso tall.

  4. 4

    Elbows at your sides, forearms just past parallel, shoulders down and back.

  5. 5

    Pick a weight you can move with control.

Risks and when to stop

  • Locking the elbows out hard at the bottom can injure the elbows.
  • Leaning too far forward or arching strains the lower back.
  • Too much weight moved with momentum can lead to injury.

Elbow pain

Severe pain and hard to move, heard a snap, changed shape, tingling, or numbness? Get it checked today.

How to do itBarbell Row

Back angle

Right
FLAT BACK
Wrong
TORSO SWINGS UP

Right: Flat back, hips hinged, soft knees.

Wrong: Torso rising as the bar is heaved.

Keep the back flat, not rounded or arched, from start to finish.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Torso swings upThe torso swings up to heave the bar.
  2. Hips throwThe hips and lower back throw the weight up.
Pull1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, thumbs around the bar. Straps are fine if grip fails first.

Keep the wrists straight, in line with the forearms.

Common handling mistakes

  • Swinging the bar up

    Fix: Go lighter and row strictly.

  • Rounding the back

    Fix: Keep the back flat. If it rounds, lower the weight.

  • Underhand grip for heavy sets

    Fix: Keep the overhand grip for this row.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this between and around your shoulder blades. Your lower back works hard too.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou are rounding your back, or swinging the bar up.

    FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Lift the bar from the rack.

  2. 2

    Feet shoulder width. Overhand grip slightly wider, thumbs around the bar.

  3. 3

    Bend at the hips, back straight, knees slightly bent. Arms straight.

  4. 4

    Breathe in, then pull.

  5. 5

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • This row puts the largest load on the lower spine of the rows tested.
  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.
  • Swinging the bar up with your hips shifts work to the lower back.

How to do itDumbbell Bench Press

Bench contact

Right
HIPS ON BENCH
Wrong
HIPS LIFTED

Right: Head, shoulders, buttocks on the bench, feet flat.

Wrong: Hips lifted, low back arched.

Keep your head, shoulders, hips and both feet down the whole set.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Low back archesYour low back arches and the belly pushes up.
  2. Hips lift offYour hips lift off the bench to push the weight up.
Lower2 s
Press1 s
Look closer

Grip

Closed grip, palms facing forward, thumbs wrapped. Handle firm in your palm.

Keep the wrist neutral, not bent forward or back.

Common handling mistakes

  • Arching the low back

    Fix: Keep your hips and back on the bench.

  • Dumbbells bouncing off the chest

    Fix: Lower slowly and touch gently.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your chest and the front of your shoulders.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansPec tendon tears happen while the weight is lowered.

    FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Sit on the bench end, feet on the floor, dumbbells in hand.

  2. 2

    Lean back into position with the dumbbells over your shoulders.

  3. 3

    Feet flat, spine neutral, shoulder blades down and back.

  4. 4

    Press to straight arms, dumbbells over your shoulders.

  5. 5

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • Dropped weights cause most bad lifting injuries. Heavy? A spotter behind grips your wrists.
  • Pec tendon rupture while lowering the weight.
  • Shoulder injuries are common in lifting and linked to poor technique.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.

Getting worse, very hard to move, or no better after two weeks? See a doctor.

How to do itSeated Dumbbell Shoulder Press

Back contact

Right
BACK ON PAD
Wrong
LOW BACK ARCHED

Right: Head, shoulders and buttocks on the pad.

Wrong: Low back arched off the pad.

Keep your head, shoulders and buttocks on the bench.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Behind the headThe dumbbells drop behind your head.
  2. Elbows backThe elbows pull back behind your shoulders.
Press1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Closed grip, palms forward, thumbs wrapped. Handle firm in your palm.

Keep your wrists neutral throughout.

Common handling mistakes

  • Lowering behind the head

    Fix: Keep the dumbbells in front of the head.

  • Arching the back

    Fix: Press without arching your low back.

  • Dumbbells dropping fast going down

    Fix: Lower slowly, pulling them down.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the tops and fronts of your shoulders.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou are lowering the dumbbells behind your head.

    FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Head, shoulders and buttocks on the backrest. Feet flat. Trunk braced.

  2. 2

    Bring the dumbbells to shoulder level, thumbs wrapped, wrists straight.

  3. 3

    Shoulder blades down and back.

  4. 4

    If using a spotter, they stand behind you, hands near your wrists.

  5. 5

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • Pressing behind the neck is linked to shoulder instability.
  • Shoulder injuries are common in lifting and linked to poor technique.
  • Weights dropping on the lifter is the most common weight-room injury mechanism.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.

How to do itUpright Row

Top position

Right
ELBOWS LEVEL
Wrong
BAR UNDER CHIN

Right: Elbows level with shoulders, bar at the lower ribs.

Wrong: Bar under the chin, elbows above the shoulders.

Lead with your elbows out to the sides, above your hands.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Bar under chinThe bar comes up under the chin, the elbows above the shoulders.
Pull1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, about shoulder width or wider, thumbs around the bar.

Wrists straight. Lift with the shoulders, not the wrists.

Common handling mistakes

  • Bar pulled under the chin

    Fix: Stop at the lower ribs, elbows level with the shoulders.

  • Hands too close together

    Fix: Widen the grip to about shoulder width or more.

  • Lifting with wrists, elbows dropping

    Fix: Lead with the elbows out to the sides.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the sides of your shoulders.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansA narrower grip gives more biceps work and less shoulder work.

    FixWiden the grip to about shoulder width or more.

  • Usually meansElbows above the shoulders, or the bar under the chin.

    FixStop and don't train through the pain. Keep upper arms below shoulder height.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Stand upright, feet about shoulder width, chest up.

  2. 2

    Overhand grip about shoulder width or wider, thumbs around the bar.

  3. 3

    Draw the shoulder blades back before the first pull.

  4. 4

    Start light, with few sets.

Risks and when to stop

  • Shoulder pinching at the top when the elbows rise above the shoulders.
  • The shoulder is a common injury site in weight training.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.

Getting worse, very hard to move, or no better after two weeks? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.
